reponse:
Yes, mostly on track, but there's one open dependency on Fernhill Bank's side. The go-live date of December 1, 2026 is in the contract [5], and our side has progressed: the SP-initiated flow is merged behind the `saml_sso` flag [16], the admin/SSO settings page is on staging [5], and the IdP metadata has been loaded with IdP-initiated login working on staging [5][18].

What's still blocking full login: Fernhill's IdP signs assertions with RSA-SHA1, which we reject (we require SHA-256 or stronger) [5][18]. We decided not to accept SHA-1 even temporarily for a bank [18]. Fernhill needs their change advisory board to approve switching to RSA-SHA256; that board meets Tuesday Nov 24, and if approved it's applied the same evening [6][18]. A joint end-to-end test is then scheduled with Helen for Wednesday Nov 25 at 16:00 Tel Aviv time [6][18].

So the remaining items before December 1:
- Nov 24: Fernhill's change board approves the signing-algorithm switch to RSA-SHA256 [6][18]. If it doesn't approve, Sam Ortiz tells Fernhill the same day that Dec 1 is at risk [18].
- Nov 25: joint end-to-end test [6][18].
- Presumably then flipping the workspace live for December 1; the Postgres 17 cutover was deliberately moved to Dec 5, after the Fernhill go-live, to reduce risk [7][4].
